aldermanic-incomplete-filings.area: Appleton, Kaukauna, Bellevue, Berlin, Brillion, Cuba City, Durand, Edgerton, New London, Port Washington
aldermanic-incomplete-filings.summary: Ten cities and villages have no aldermanic districts on the map because their counties' ward filings leave some or most wards unassigned, so their district lines cannot be drawn honestly.
aldermanic-incomplete-filings.why: The districts are unions of wards, and the state's ward file is only as complete as each county's filing. Where a filing codes a fraction of a city's wards, drawing just that fraction would show fragments as if they were the whole plan.
aldermanic-incomplete-filings.wanted: For one of the ten: a county ward filing that assigns every city ward its district, or the city's own district boundary file. Appleton is the largest — its county coding the wards, or the city publishing its map as data, would close it.

alderperson-rosters.summary: In most of the 155 municipalities with districts on the map, the card names your district but not the council member holding it. Six big cities name their alderpersons; the rest link nothing yet.
alderperson-rosters.why: Wisconsin has no statewide roster of municipal council members — the league of municipalities keeps its directory member-gated — so each city's roster must be read from its own site, one pinned scraper at a time.
alderperson-rosters.wanted: For any city or village with districts on the map: a page pairing each aldermanic or trustee district with the member holding it. A statewide open roster of municipal officials would close this gap wholesale.

county-officials.summary: In 50 of Wisconsin's 72 counties the card names your board district but not the supervisor holding it, and links the county board instead.
county-officials.why: Wisconsin publishes every county's district lines in one file but no statewide roster of the people in them. Twenty-two counties publish a readable district-keyed list, and those ship; the rest publish maps, PDFs, or nothing readable.
county-officials.wanted: For one of the 52 unnamed counties: a page listing each supervisory district beside the supervisor holding it. A district map, a PDF or an alphabetical list with no district column cannot be used.

madison-tid-undrawn.summary: One of Madison's fifteen active tax districts is missing from the map — the state certified TID 55 as active in 2025, but the city has not yet published its boundary, so a reader inside it is told they are in no TID.
madison-tid-undrawn.why: The card can only draw what the city publishes as geometry. The state's certified active list and the city's own TIF program page both carry the district; the city's boundary layer does not yet.
madison-tid-undrawn.wanted: TID 55's boundary in the city's open-data TIF layer — the next operator rebuild ships it the moment it appears, and the builder's pin guarantees the change gets a human look.

ng911-ems-filings.area: Iowa, Jefferson, Langlade, Vilas and Walworth counties
ng911-ems-filings.summary: In five counties the EMS card can name no service, because their 911 authorities' EMS-boundary filings are absent from the state's NG911 aggregate.
ng911-ems-filings.why: The statewide layer is the Office of Emergency Communications' aggregate of each county 911 authority's own filing, and it can only carry what a county files — no other statewide publisher of who-is-dispatched-here boundaries exists.
ng911-ems-filings.wanted: The missing counties' EMS-boundary filings reaching the OEC aggregate — the state's roughly weekly refresh carries them the moment a county files.

ng911-law-filings.area: Iowa, Langlade, Vilas and Walworth counties, plus part of Polk
ng911-law-filings.summary: In four counties the law-enforcement card can name no agency, and in part of Polk County only some agencies, because those 911 authorities' law-boundary filings are absent or partial in the state's NG911 aggregate.
ng911-law-filings.why: The statewide layer is the Office of Emergency Communications' aggregate of each county 911 authority's own filing, and it can only carry what a county files — no other statewide publisher of who-serves-here boundaries exists.
ng911-law-filings.wanted: The missing or completed law-boundary filings reaching the OEC aggregate — the state's roughly weekly refresh carries them the moment a county files.

rusd-school-board.summary: Racine Unified is the only Wisconsin school board besides Milwaukee's elected by geographic district, and its nine district boundaries aren't on the map — the district publishes them only as picture maps, not as data.
rusd-school-board.why: Statute names exactly two districted school boards in the state. Milwaukee's ships because its city publishes real geometry; Racine Unified publishes its election districts only as map documents no program can read as boundaries.
rusd-school-board.wanted: RUSD's nine election-district boundaries as data — a shapefile or feature service from the district, or its map republished with coordinates.

ward-polling-places.area: Wisconsin — statewide outside Milwaukee and Madison
ward-polling-places.summary: Outside Milwaukee and Madison the ward card names your ward but not your polling place — the state publishes the pairing only through a per-address lookup, never as a dataset this project has located, so the card links that lookup instead.
ward-polling-places.why: Polling places are assigned per ward by each municipality, and no county or state source publishes the statewide ward-to-polling-place pairing as open data this project can read and verify.
ward-polling-places.wanted: A statewide or per-county dataset pairing each ward with its polling place and street address, published as data rather than behind a lookup form — a per-election spreadsheet from the state or a county clerk would work.
